name: pricing
description: Pricing table composing card tiers with the stat primitive for the price, a badge for the highlight, separators, icon-ticked feature lists, and one call-to-action per tier. Composition only: zero JavaScript, no controller, no reactive directives. A highlighted tier is data-state='featured' on the tier card.

heading.description: Section heading. Give it an id and point the section's aria-labelledby at it

description.description: Optional intro paragraph. Must be a direct child of the section — the tiers' own card descriptions are card slots, not this one

tiers.description: The tier grid. Column count comes from data-cols on the root, not from a nested grid component

tier.description: One plan — a nested data-ui='card'. Inside a tier you address the CARD's slots (header, title, description, body, footer), never pricing's: the nearest data-ui ancestor owns a data-part

footnote.description: Fine print under the tiers (taxes, cancellation, currency)

featured.description: Highlights one tier with a primary ring. Pair it with an in-content badge ('Most popular') so the emphasis is not colour-only

required_attrs: aria-labelledby on the section pointing at the heading id
aria-labelledby on each tier pointing at that tier's title id
aria-hidden='true' on the decorative feature tick icons
the featured tier states its emphasis in text, not only with colour

keyboard.Tab: move through the tier call-to-action links in source order

templates.html:
{heading}

{description}

{tier_name}

{tier_blurb}

{price}
{period}
  • {feature}
{cta}

{footnote}

notes: Slot ownership: a data-part belongs to its nearest data-ui ancestor. Inside a tier that ancestor is the card, so the price/features live in the card's header and body slots and pricing addresses them contextually in CSS. Adding a pricing-specific data-part inside a tier makes it an orphan part of the card and `faqir audit` flags it.
The price is a nested data-ui='stat' (value = amount, label = period). Pricing re-orders the stat label so the amount leads.
`faqir scaffold landing-page` copies the block between the <!-- @ui:scaffold landing-page --> markers in pricing.html verbatim.

changes.note: The responsive ladder moves onto the breakpoint canon, mobile-first (task 0.8-09). The sheet's max-width media blocks became min-width floors on canon tiers (sm 40rem/640px, md 48rem/768px, lg 64rem/1024px), so every unconditional rule is now the PHONE case and a tier block only ever widens it. The tier grid follows grid's mobile-first semantics (0.8-04): data-cols names the WIDEST count, reached at lg, with two columns from sm and one on a phone. The floors keep their values, so the only behavioural shift is at exactly a floor: 1024px now gets the wide layout rather than the narrow one.
